title: Sheafified quotient-valued dual Koszul homology has the increasing wedge frame
statement: Let i:Z\to Y be a closed immersion of schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-closed-immersion], U an affine open, A=\Gamma(Y,U), I=ker(i)(U) [def-sbc-closed-immersion-ideal-sheaf], and n,m natural numbers. Let f:Fin(m)\to A generate I. Let K be the explicit quotient-valued signed dual Koszul cochain complex with K^p=Hom_A(\wedge^p A^m,A/I) and differential signed precomposition by the Koszul boundary [new-j3-koszul-quotient-coefficient-complex]. Let T be associated-module sheafification followed by restriction along the spectrum isomorphism U\simeq Spec(A) [lem-weil-pbc-spec-module-tilde-sections]. Then T(H^n(K)) is isomorphic to the restriction to U of the coproduct of copies of B=i_*O_Z indexed by ULift of n-element subsets of Fin(m) [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-pc-module-pullback]. No Koszul regularity or derived-category hypothesis is needed.

source.place: Lemma 48.15.4, proof: the quotient-valued Hom complex has zero differential and its cohomology is the Hom from the corresponding Koszul term.

proof.text: Use the explicit contraction formula for the Koszul differential. On a decomposable wedge the boundary is a sum of wedges with coefficients sign times linearCombination(f,v_j). Each coefficient lies in I. Applying any A-linear map into A/I therefore kills each summand, so signed precomposition is zero. Non-successor differentials vanish by the complex shape. ShortComplex.HomologyData.ofZeros identifies homology with its middle term.

Use the exterior-power basis of the standard finite free module, reindexed by ULift. Module.Basis.constr identifies functionals with their values on this basis, and Finsupp.linearEquivFunOnFinite turns these functions into finitely supported functions. ModuleCat.finsuppCoconeIsColimit identifies this module with the coproduct of A/I. Map the isomorphism by T and use PreservesCoproduct.iso.

On the affine chart the closed immersion gives a surjection A to Gamma(i inverse U) with kernel I. Its kernel-lift ring equivalence and the source affine spectrum isomorphism give a compatible presentation i inverse U as Spec(A/I); compatibility follows from toSpecGamma naturality. Apply affine_quotient_restricted_iso to identify T(A/I) with B restricted to U. Apply Sigma.mapIso to these identifications and the inverse coproduct-preservation comparison for ordinary open restriction.

lean.statement:
theorem koszul_quotient_homology_frame
    {Z Y : Scheme.{u}} (i : Z ⟶ Y) [IsClosedImmersion i]
    (U : Y.affineOpens) (n m : ℕ) (f : Fin m → Γ(Y, U.1))
    (hf : Ideal.span (Set.range f) = i.ker.ideal U) :
    let B := (Scheme.Modules.pushforward i).obj (SheafOfModules.unit Z.ringCatSheaf)
    let T := tilde.functor Γ(Y, U.1) ⋙ Scheme.Modules.restrictFunctor U.2.isoSpec.hom
    let Q := (ExteriorAlgebra.koszulQuotientDualComplex
      (Γ(Y, U.1) : Type u) (i.ker.ideal U) m f).homology n
    Nonempty (T.obj Q ≅ (Scheme.Modules.restrictFunctor U.1.ι).obj
      (∐ fun _ : ULift.{u} (Set.powersetCard (Fin m) n) ↦ B))
